Low evening sun rakes the whole length of the house almost level, so the hazed air goes hot apricot while the ribs and the wet iron underfoot stay slate-blue. Palette: apricot against slate-blue.

The light comes down through layer after layer of leaf-shaded glass and the whole interior swims in jade and bottle-green, with one bright lemon-yellow patch on the wet grating where a pane is bare. Palette: jade and lemon-yellow.

Dusk, and the gas mantles are lit: warm amber glowing in a row along the catwalk and the beds beneath them, the panes overhead gone deep peacock-blue with the last of the sky. Palette: amber against peacock-blue.

A storm is running down the glass. Flat pewter-grey daylight fills everything, the water sheeting on the panes catches a hard silver shine, and the boiler's open firedoor throws one small orange pool onto the wet floor. Palette: pewter-silver against orange.
Full noon straight overhead: the steam in the high air blazes white and the whole house below it goes saturated emerald with deep teal in every shadow. Palette: white and emerald.

First sun, low and rose-gold, comes in almost level and lies in long pools along the wet grating, while the far end of the house is still cold lavender with night. Palette: rose-gold against lavender.

Snow is banked on the outside of the panes and the light through it is soft blue-white like frosted milk; inside, the hot-water pipes glow and light the nearest leaves warm ochre from below. Palette: blue-white against ochre.
Sun comes through the steam in broad soft shafts of dusty gold, strikes the pool, and bounces a shifting turquoise ripple-light up onto the iron ribs overhead. Palette: dusty gold and turquoise.

Late side-light comes in low through the glazed flank so every leaf is honey on one side and cool slate-violet on the other, and the whole house is built out of those two colours. Palette: honey against slate-violet.

Overcast pearl-grey daylight floods in evenly from every direction, and the only colour in the place is the planting itself: acid-green new fronds and one bed of hot scarlet blooms. Palette: pearl-grey with acid-green and scarlet.

Sunset burns at the far end wall and the whole house fills with tangerine haze, the ribs black against it, while a cool mint-green glow leaks in behind from the cold-house through the inner glass. Palette: tangerine against mint-green.
Moonlight and gaslight together: every wet pane above holds silver-blue, and warm brass-amber pools low around the lamps along the bed edges. Palette: silver-blue against brass-amber.

A lamplit night inspection: pools of warm sodium-gold under each hanging lamp, deep bottle-green dark in between, and the steam curling up bright through each lamp's cone of light. Palette: sodium-gold against bottle-green.

Rain has just stopped and the glass above is beaded, breaking the sun into hundreds of soft bright points; the house beneath is washed cool aquamarine with warm russet on the brick floor. Palette: aquamarine against russet.

The shade blinds are half drawn, so the light arrives in broad warm cream where the panes are still clear and cool sage-green where the blind filters it, the two meeting in a soft line across the beds. Palette: cream against sage-green.
Deep viridian shade under the fern tiers, and down through the one open vent comes a single hot shaft of white-gold that lands on the wet stone and steams. Palette: viridian and white-gold.
Low winter sun through frosted glass leaves the whole house pale gold and ivory with lilac shadows, and the steam standing off every pipe joint is lit bright. Palette: pale gold against lilac.

Night at the boiler end: one hot orange glow out of the open firedoor lights the undersides of the leaves and the drifting steam, and everything beyond it lies cool indigo. Palette: orange against indigo.
A heat-haze afternoon, the high air thick and the light gone peach and dusty, while the pool below throws a cool green counter-light up into the roof. Palette: peach against cool green.
The sky has cleared hard and clean after a downpour: sharp cobalt showing through the wet panes and everything inside bright glossy grass-green. Palette: cobalt and grass-green.
A hot copper-pink dawn glows through the end glass and lies flat along the wet nave floor, while the roof overhead is still deep blue-grey. Palette: copper-pink against blue-grey.
Midday comes through leaf and steam all dappled, hundreds of small warm yellow patches shifting on the wet grating and the air above them soft milky white. Palette: warm yellow and milky white.

Thin cirrus across the sun turns the light silver-white and flat, every leaf surface equally lit, while the copper feed-pipes running the length of the beds catch the diffuse glow and hold a long dull rose along their curves. Palette: silver-white against dull rose.

The vent flaps have been open all night and cold blue-grey air has settled low; now the morning gas jets warm the planting tier by tier, and the lowest leaves glow bright citrine while the upper glass stays cold and dark. Palette: citrine against blue-grey.

Fog has pressed itself against every pane and the light is sourceless, white and absolutely even, so the only shadows are the dark grey ribs and the deep burgundy clay at the bed edges. Palette: white against grey and burgundy.

Afternoon thunder-light, green-yellow and strange, presses through the glass and stains the steam that rises from the pool a sickly chartreuse, the brass fittings below it going briefly electric. Palette: chartreuse and brass-yellow.

The blind on the south flank is drawn full across and the light that makes it through is the colour of old beeswax, warm and dull gold, pooling soft on the stone floor with no edge anywhere. Palette: beeswax gold.

Ice has filmed the outer panes overnight and the morning light refracts into faint brief rainbows that travel the length of the floor as the sun climbs, the rest of the house a quiet neutral grey. Palette: rainbow prismatic against neutral grey.

The coal smoke has backed inside through the flue and a brown-amber haze sits in the high vault, filtering the sky to raw sienna overhead while the air below it stays its usual warm steam-white. Palette: raw sienna against steam-white.

Candles on the inspection barrow cast a low unsteady pool of tallow-yellow that reaches only the nearest bed edge, leaving the surrounding glass and iron in deep cool charcoal. Palette: tallow-yellow against charcoal.

Reflected sunlight from the whitewashed end wall throws a second soft light in from the east face, so the house is lit both ways at once: direct warm gold from the west, bounced chalk-white from the east. Palette: gold against chalk-white.

A single vent is open at the ridge and cold outer air pours through it in a thin pale stream, visible as a blue-white plume against the general warm ochre-brown steam filling the nave. Palette: blue-white against ochre-brown.

The gas has been turned low for the night and the mantles burn the faintest possible coral-amber, enough only to warm the iron rib directly below each one; the rest of the house is cool charcoal and shadow. Palette: coral-amber against charcoal.

Midsummer noon and the sun is straight through the ridge glass, so a corridor of intense white-gold runs the centre of the house while both flanks stay deep submerged green. Palette: white-gold against submerged green.

Autumn outside and the panes are full of the red-orange colour of the deciduous trees behind the wall, that borrowed warmth filling the interior with a soft terracotta haze, the plants inside briefly the same shade as the beds. Palette: terracotta and warm orange.

Firefly-pale phosphorescence, lit by the reflected glow of the hot-house boiler on a bank of low cloud outside, fills the curved roof with a diffuse rose-lilac, and the inside of the glass holds it like a lamp shade. Palette: rose-lilac above warm orange.

The aquifer water coming through the new lead pipes runs cold and the pipe sweat has beaded and drips onto the floor, each drop catching the high noon light as a hard diamond-white point against the cool blue of the wet stone. Palette: diamond-white against cool blue.

Predawn: only the pilot light in the boiler burns, a small steady ultramarine-edged orange point in the deep black of the far end, all the glass above it pure midnight-blue with reflected starfield. Palette: orange against midnight-blue.

Heavy morning dew on the inside of the cold-house panes runs in sheets and the glass has gone the milky blue of mother-of-pearl; the wet wooden staging beneath it shines dark walnut-brown in the same diffuse light. Palette: mother-of-pearl blue against walnut.

A late spring afternoon with the sky half violet from approaching rain and half clear lemon: both colours press through the glass at once and lay their stripe across the beds, violet to the north, lemon to the south. Palette: violet against lemon.

Thick tropical planting has closed the upper tier and the light reaching the floor has been filtered to a dark pool-green, still and deep, with occasional bright points of copper-gold where leaf gaps align. Palette: pool-green against copper-gold.

The iron ribs have been newly painted and the wet black paint doubles the reflection of the gaslight below into the glass above, so the whole vault is lined with paired amber commas on deep blue-black. Palette: amber against blue-black.

High-summer haze on the outer glass bleaches the daylight to a flat magnolia-cream that reaches every corner equally, the only warm note the terracotta-red of the old flowerpots stacked against the back wall. Palette: magnolia-cream against terracotta-red.

The boiler has been drawn and the heat is fading; the air inside has cooled enough to show the cold glass panes in a pale pewter-blue while the last warmth in the pipes throws a faint blush of rose along the low staging. Palette: pewter-blue against rose.

Sleet is half-melting on the outer face of the glass and running in grey rivulets, the light through them striped silver and dark; on the grating below, one burst of scarlet from the heating coils flushes the immediate wet iron. Palette: silver-grey against scarlet.

Just before the gas lamps are lit, the interior holds the last of the sky in a long blue twilight, every iron rib a near-black line against it and the water in the pool below a flat pewter-mirror of the same blue. Palette: blue twilight against pewter.

The outer roller blinds on the east side are half raised and the bars of morning light they let in fall across the beds at a steep angle, each bar a solid warm saffron stripe with cool steel-blue between them. Palette: saffron against steel-blue.

Thin cirrus covers the sun so the light arrives shadowless and cool silver-white, and every wet leaf holds its own small mirror; the only warmth is the faint copper gleam along the boiler pipe running the length of the far wall. Palette: silver-white against copper.

The east panes catch the climbing morning sun and go bright beaten gold while the west side of every rib and pot and leaf-edge stays in cool grey-mauve shadow, the house cut cleanly down its long axis. Palette: beaten gold against grey-mauve.

Fog has pressed against the outer glass all day and the diffused light inside is a flat, even oyster-white; the one contrast is the deep Brunswick-green of the massed leaves massed low. Palette: oyster-white against Brunswick-green.

A single vent in the ridge is open and cold blue air streams in, making the warm interior steam roll and glow; where the steam thins the light turns clear straw-yellow, where it thickens it goes milky violet. Palette: straw-yellow against milky violet.

The afternoon sun hits the iron ribs at a hard angle and they cast long parallel shadows across the gravel beds, the lit strips bright cinnamon, the shadow strips a deep cool prussian-blue. Palette: cinnamon against prussian-blue.

Evening cloud breaks just at the horizon and a band of raw magenta crosses the low end wall, reflected once in the long pool below so the magenta doubles against the surrounding deep charcoal of the roof. Palette: magenta against charcoal.

Ice on the outer panes at dawn: the risen sun turns each crystal to a burning point of light and the whole roof blazes like hammered silver, while the floor beneath stays cold violet-grey. Palette: silver against violet-grey.

The shade blinds are fully drawn on the south flank and the light is cool and filtered, a flat sage colour everywhere, except where steam rises through a crack in the blind into hard raw cream. Palette: sage against raw cream.

A brief hailstorm whitens the roof and the light through it turns brilliant chalk-white, pressing down on the leaf canopy and giving every upper frond a sharp lime-green edge. Palette: chalk-white against lime-green.

The autumn sun is low enough to clear the near wall and strike the far interior end directly, lighting the brick and the pots there in deep terra-cotta, while the middle of the house rests in cool blue-green half-light. Palette: terra-cotta against blue-green.

Gas is low and the mantles burn just above extinction, their light a thin wan amber; the panes above hold the violet of a clear cold night, and the two colours barely meet across the dark interior. Palette: wan amber against violet.

Just before sunrise the sky above the glass is a long gradient from deep indigo at the crown to pale rose at the horizon, and the interior holds it all reflected in the still pool surface. Palette: indigo into pale rose.

High summer, the blinds on all sides drawn against heat: the light that seeps through is golden-brown like weak tea, warm and diffuse, and the planting below sits in deep hunter-green shadow. Palette: golden-brown against hunter-green.

The pipe work at the ridge leaks steam in short puffs and each puff catches the slant sun and burns briefly bright gamboge before dissolving into the grey-green air of the canopy. Palette: gamboge against grey-green.

A partial eclipse passes over: the light drops to a strange flat bronze and every shadow sharpens and cools to slate, the two colours completely without softness or transition. Palette: bronze against slate.

The outer glass on the north flank is thick with condensation and the light from that side is blue and diffused like shallow seawater; the south light still cuts through clear in warm gilded shafts. Palette: seawater-blue against gilded.

Lamps left burning at the far end overnight: at the boiler end only cool blue pre-dawn grey enters through the glass above while the lamp glow holds a concentrated warm saffron in the distance. Palette: cool grey against saffron.

Wind is pushing clouds fast across a winter sky and the light inside pulses: a beat of flat ash-white, a beat of brief honey-gold, alternating across the wet grating in slow rhythm. Palette: ash-white against honey-gold.

New whitewash on the outer glass for summer shading turns the incoming light soft and matte, the whole interior an even warm cream-white except where the scraper has missed and one clear pane throws a hard bright lozenge of pure gold. Palette: cream-white against gold.

The low boiler-end fire has burned to a bed of deep red-orange coals and its glow replaces the faded daylight as evening comes, the leaf undersides lit red-bronze and the far glass a deep prussian-teal. Palette: red-bronze against prussian-teal.

Spring morning with the rain still on the glass: the sun behind it turns every drop to white fire and the interior below is caught between that blaze above and the cool aqua of the flooded gravel beds. Palette: white fire against aqua.

Thick tree shadow from outside falls across the south face at midday and the light through those panes is a deep filtered green, while the unshaded north glass floods the other half of the house in pure pale platinum. Palette: deep green against platinum.

The end doors stand open to a still summer evening and soft mauve dusk enters from outside, meeting the residual warm golden-tan glow of the afternoon still held in the brickwork and the clay pots. Palette: mauve against golden-tan.

Midsummer dawn at its shortest: the sky goes from dark to full light so fast the glass scarcely dims, and the interior wakes in a clean even rose-peach that the wet iron floor takes up and holds. Palette: rose-peach throughout.

A single shaft of noon light descends through a gap in the climbing foliage, strikes a brass tap on the standpipe, and scatters a ring of small bright gold points across the surrounding deep shadow-green of the bed. Palette: bright gold against shadow-green.

Thin cloud veils the midday sun so the light is even and cool, the whole house holding a single flat silver-green tone, and the brass fittings along the pipe-run catch the diffuse glow and gleam soft gold against it. Palette: silver-green against soft gold.

Frost on the outer glass has turned every pane into a scattering lens and the interior is washed in cold blue-violet, while the geothermal vent near the centre bleeds up a slow warm saffron stain through the mist. Palette: blue-violet against saffron.

The east-facing clerestory catches the last of the afternoon and pours a rich persimmon light down one wall only, leaving the opposite flank in cool grey-green shadow so the house reads as two entirely different climates. Palette: persimmon against grey-green.

High summer haze sits outside and the light arriving through the crown glass is dense and warm, a saturated gamboge filling the upper air while the brick beds below stay brick-red, unlit, in their own shadow. Palette: gamboge against brick-red.

Autumn afternoon and the low sun comes in through amber-tinted old panes at the gable, washing the stone floor in a deep burnt-sienna pool that fades slowly to cool grey-blue at the far end. Palette: burnt-sienna fading to grey-blue.

The gas is turned low for the night and the mantles emit only a faint warm rose-copper, barely enough to outline the nearest ribs, while the sky through the panes above is a deep cold prussian-blue. Palette: rose-copper against prussian-blue.

An eclipse dims the glass overhead to a strange flat bronze, shadows vanish, the whole glasshouse interior falls uniform tawny-gold, and the only cooler note is the pale celadon of the lily-tank water. Palette: tawny-gold against celadon.

Spring midmorning, clouds moving fast outside: the light pulses between bright chrome-yellow and cool pewter-white every few seconds, the wet leaves flickering between warmth and neutrality in the same rhythm. Palette: chrome-yellow and pewter-white.

The inner door to the cool-house stands open and drags a wedge of cold lilac-grey daylight across the floor while the warm house beyond it holds its deep amber-bronze, the two lights fighting at the threshold. Palette: lilac-grey against amber-bronze.

Reflected light off the pool has climbed the north-facing glass and painted a slow-moving caustic of pale sea-green on the ribs overhead, the rest of the upper house sitting in warm buff shadow. Palette: sea-green against buff.

Steam has condensed on every iron rib and each one beads and drips, catching the morning sun as a line of hard bright silver along its crown against the deep forest-green of the foliage behind. Palette: bright silver against forest-green.

Smoke from a slow-burning coke charge drifts thin and pale across the nave at mid-height, catching the daylight as a soft mauve-grey wash and separating the bright upper panes from the dark wet floor below. Palette: mauve-grey between bright glass and dark floor.

Late February and the sun is just strong enough to warm the glass: the exterior panes carry a thin blush of rose where condensation is drying and inside the light is still a cool wintry bone-white. Palette: rose against bone-white.

The cistern at the high end is overflowing very slowly and the sheet of water running down the back wall catches the afternoon light as a sheet of hammered platinum, bright against the damp terracotta behind. Palette: platinum against terracotta.

Afternoon thunderclouds have turned the sky purple-grey outside and the glasshouse interior has gone a strange bruised plum in the upper air, while the lamp above the propagating bench holds a tight island of warm gold below. Palette: plum against warm gold.

A bonfire is burning in the yard beyond the end glass and its orange flicker comes through the panes as a restless warm bronze trembling across the floor, the panes themselves each holding a small dancing ember-light. Palette: bronze and ember-orange.

First light before the sun clears the wall: indirect sky-light only, the whole house a cool even cerulean, and the white gravel paths between the beds glow faint pearl, the only things with any brightness. Palette: cerulean and pearl.

The linen shade-cloth has been rolled out along the south face and the light through it is soft, dense and green-tinged, like being inside a tent; the exposed ridge at the top lets in one stripe of raw white. Palette: tent-green against raw white.

A calm clear evening after harvest, the gas not yet lit: the interior holds the last of the day as a warm dusty rose, the ironwork overhead silhouetted against a sky going from rose to deep violet at the crown. Palette: dusty rose against deep violet.

The coal-hod has been left near the open firedoor and its black iron holds a rim of fierce red-orange from the coals, the heat shimmer above it bending the cool teal light of the glass behind into ribbons. Palette: red-orange against teal.

Morning mist outside thickens the glass to opacity so the light is sourceless and diffuse, a pure warm cream from every direction, and the only contrast in the whole house is the wet black iron of the pipes. Palette: warm cream against wet black.

The vent flaps have been cranked fully open along the ridge and a column of hot white steam drives straight up through each one into a bright blue winter sky, the blue reading cool down inside the open throat. Palette: hot white and clear blue.

Candles have been set in the beds for a late-season heat against frost: dozens of small flame-points at floor level, warm straw-yellow, and above them the cold glass holds a deep ink-blue reflection of the sky. Palette: straw-yellow against ink-blue.

The iron ribs are freshly painted and the white paint catches the grey morning light so the structure reads bright against the dark olive of the massed foliage, reversing the usual relationship of frame to green. Palette: bright white against dark olive.

Side raking light from a gap in cloud catches the standing moisture in the air and turns the whole nave into a corridor of luminous warm topaz, the steam going solid with colour and the shadows beneath it cool grey-green. Palette: topaz against grey-green.

Thin cirrus dims the afternoon sun just enough to soften it: the light falls pearl-white through the high panes, and where it strikes the copper irrigation pipes it throws a warm blush-pink gleam along the whole run of the beds. Palette: pearl-white against blush-pink.

Fog has pressed close against the outside of the glass and the daylight through it is a flat, even silver-lilac, sourceless and quiet; only the bare clay beds hold any warmth, showing dark umber against the cold panes. Palette: silver-lilac against umber.

The vent louvers are open and a shaft of raw afternoon sky comes straight down blue and hard, cutting through the steam cloud and leaving it lit cerulean on one side, deep charcoal on the other. Palette: cerulean against charcoal.
